newsitem.title: USA: NATO chief makes pledge on Bosnia war trials.
newsitem.headline: NATO chief makes pledge on Bosnia war trials.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana gave his personal commitment on Thursday that indicted Bosnian war criminals will face an international tribunal before the international community leaves the area.
"It is my personal commitment that war criminals will be where they should be, that means in front of the tribunal, before the international community leaves Bosnia," Solana told reporters.
He stressed, however, that arrests of indicted war criminals would be made by international forces in Bosnia only when tactically possible.

"If you meet a war criminal surrounded by 100 people...then you have no obligation to arrest," Solana said. However, he noted that sealed indictments against war criminals allowed for better preparation for arrests.
Solana noted that one indicted war criminal had been arrested and another killed this month in the Prijedor region.

"I think this policy...has opened a new dynamic and we have to use it in an intelligent manner," he said. "I think that the situation in Pale now, due to this operation, this Prijedor case, is going to change."
He declined to elaborate on what changes might take place, and said no new guidelines were needed to govern the arrests of indicted war criminals.
